input:
You are king_e1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 36. the team planned Kd4 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kc4 instead, and that move was played, walking into a forced mate.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 7. the team planned Qc2 (queen_d1), but queen_d1 (amnesia) sent Qb3 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 15. the team planned Bf4 (bishop_c1), but queen_d1 (greed) sent Qxd4 instead, and that move was played, costing 756 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send only your piece's move if you are the chosen piece; if you are not the chosen piece, stay silent unless the plan explicitly names you, and never send a capture or retreat on your own initiative even if your piece is attacked or a capture is available.
- Before sending any move, confirm that the move you are about to send is exactly the move named in the latest plan message and that your piece is the one named; if the plan names a different piece or move, send nothing, even if your piece can capture or is attacked, and if the plan names your piece, send only the planned move and re-read it right before sending.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending, write out in chat the planned move's exact square pair (e.g. 'king e1 to d4'), compare it character-by-character to the move you are about to send, and if they differ in any way, do not send it.", "covers": ["amnesia", "greed", "panic"]}
